data.text: The locked result is composite 10.4, band 3, routed to committee. The largest driver is the third-party channel. The due-diligence control CTL-T01 was overridden to 4.5 because the audit predates the corridor arrangement. The corridor review is only planned, with an auditor review scheduled for Nov 2026 and a scope letter attached, so it is not yet evidenced. The corpus also has no clause for cash-pickup agent networks. Recommended outcome: approve_with_conditions, with the corridor review filed before go-live, and the policy gap tracked and resolved.
File the completed corridor due-diligence review covering the new arrangement.
Complete the planned corridor due-diligence review with the auditor.
Define policy coverage and interim oversight for cash-pickup agent networks.

The change is recommended for approval with conditions. The payout partner's due-diligence review does not yet cover the new corridor arrangement. The auditor's review is scheduled for Nov 2026, and the scope letter is attached. The bank also has no written standard yet for cash-pickup agent networks. Before go-live: file the completed corridor review from the auditor. Within three months: work with the compliance team to set oversight rules for cash-pickup agents.

No evidence of those checks is on file. No actions are assigned to you at this time. The analyst will contact you if more information is needed.

The payout partner onboarding for the El Salvador corridor is recommended for approval with conditions. The largest driver of the composite assessment is the channel risk. No planned controls, policy gaps, or overridden controls are recorded in this submission. Without additional detail on the partner's due-diligence status, agent vetting procedures, or transaction monitoring capabilities, evidence of control effectiveness across the vendor onboarding lifecycle cannot be confirmed. The analyst should verify that anti-money-laundering checks, sanctions screening, and ongoing monitoring align with the El Salvador corridor's requirements before go-live.
Complete partner due-diligence review for El Salvador corridor, including beneficial ownership and sanctions screening
Confirm agent vetting and ongoing transaction monitoring procedures are in place and tested

The payout partner onboarding for the El Salvador corridor is approved with conditions. The partner's due-diligence review must be completed and filed before go-live, including full beneficial ownership verification and sanctions screening. Before go-live, confirm that agent vetting and transaction monitoring procedures are operational and have been tested. These steps ensure the bank can meet its anti-money-laundering obligations across the El Salvador corridor.
